title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency and throughput) vs baseline provider. Redwood team presented optimized runs using batching, KV cache and quantization profiles. Customer raised questions about VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS, and cost per 1k tokens. Agreed next steps: share full benchmark CSV, security pack, updated cost estimate, schedule exec review in two weeks and run a final production-like stress test.
action_items: Alex Mercer: Share full benchmark CSV and runbook (due 2026-08-02)
Priya Nair: Provide tuned config used for quantized runs + autoscale policy (due 2026-08-04)
Diego Ramos: Send SOC2 and KMS integration docs + contact for security review (due 2026-08-03)
Samir Gupta: Provision test dataset and schedule production-like stress test (due 2026-08-07)
next_steps: Redwood to upload raw benchmark CSV and annotated notes to shared folder
Customer to confirm exec review date (2 weeks out)
Run dedicated cluster stress test with 10% higher qps than baseline
Share updated cost estimate for Dedicated and Hosted with KV caching applied
Security team to review SOC2 + KMS docs and reply with any blockers
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-31 10:00 PDT / Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex (AE), Priya (SE), Diego (CSM)  Nimbus: Samir (ML), Jill (CTO), Lena (CloudOps), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda  go over the benchmark numbers vs baseline cloud, discuss tuning we did this week, any security gaps, and then next steps. is that right?
[00:12] Jill: yep, that's perfect. we got a few execs asking for a clean gap number on p95 latency and tokens per dollar so we'll want that.
[00:20] Priya: Great, i'll start with the headline. We ran three profiles this week: hosted default, hosted with KV caching + batching, and a quantized run on dedicated. compared to your baseline provider (BaselineCloud), p95 latency dropped ~18% on the KV-cached runs and throughput improved about 1.6x at the same GPU footprint.
[00:38] Samir: can you remind which model variant you were using? we have our internal guidance for the 13B family.
[00:45] Priya: yeah we used rdx-13b-v3 (note: our label, might show as rdx13bv3 on the export), the baseline used baseline-13b-oc, which seems to have higher mem copy overhead. also the baseline runs didn't have prefix cache enabled.
[01:05] Tom: When you say 1.6x throughput, what was QPS and batch size?
[01:12] Priya: baseline was ~120 qps with batch size 1 steady state. With batching + dynamic batching we hit ~190 qps with median batch sizes around 4 to 6 depending on tail. latency p95 for the KV-cached hosted was 210ms vs baseline 255ms on your test script.
[01:30] Alex: Important to call out that we used continuous batching and tweaked the autoscale policy to keep cold starts at bay. that made a big difference for tail latency.
[01:40] Samir: any differences when you moved to quantized on dedicated? memory savings, obviously, but did that impact latency?
[01:48] Priya: Good Q. Quantized dedicated gave lower GPU memory and lower cost per token. raw token generation latency was slightly higher on single-threaded runs because of kernel differences, but when we increase parallelism throughput improved markedly  p95 sat around 230ms but throughput jumped to ~240 qps on the dedicated 8-GPU pool.
[02:10] Jill: so summarizing: hosted KV-cached = best p95, dedicated quantized = best throughput/cost. correct?
[02:18] Priya: generally yes. it's a tradeoff: hosted cached minimizes observable latency for user-facing requests; dedicated quantized helps unit economics if you have steady throughput.
[02:30] Lena: there's also the VPC question. Our security team wants private control plane or at least VPC peering and HSM for keys. how mature is your private offering?
[02:42] Alex: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem control plane and KMS/HSM integrations. i'll send the SOC2 pack and the KMS integration guide after this call. Diego, that's on you to attach?
[02:55] Diego: Yup i'll drop the security bundle into the shared folder. also i'll include a template SOW for Dedicated if you want to move forward.
[03:06] Tom: Any unexpected errors in the runs? we saw some 500s in earlier test runs from baseline when we ramped, did you see anything?
[03:14] Priya: We saw very few 5xx's, mostly from an initial autoscaler misconfig which we fixed. baseline showed a rise in tail errors when qps spiked due to smaller effective batching. our runs were smoothed by the cache and batching.
[03:30] Samir: can you share the exact command and flags you used for the quantized run and the autoscale policy? we want to reproduce.
[03:36] Priya: Absolutely. i'll push the exact config: quantize=aq8, kernel-set=opt3, batch-window-ms=30, dynamic-batching=true, prefix-cache-ttl=10m. note transcription might show 'aq8' as 'a q eight' in the export.
[03:55] Jill: On cost: what's order of magnitude difference per 1k tokens vs our baseline?
[04:02] Alex: Roughly speaking, on the quantized dedicated config it's about 30-40% less per 1k tokens compared to baseline when you normalize for throughput and assume prefix caching. hosted cached sits in the middle but the p95 advantage can be worth the extra cost for customer-facing flows.
[04:20] Lena: For compliance, our data retention policy requires logs to be retained 2 years and audit trails  can Redwood accommodate longer retention or push logs to our SIEM?
[04:29] Diego: Yes we support pushing audit logs to your syslogs/SIEM and can extend retention on enterprise tiers. i'll include retention SLA options in the pack.
[04:40] Tom: we want to run a production-like stress test that simulates 200 qps sustained with 10% higher load spikes. can Redwood support that with Dedicated?
[04:49] Priya: yes, we'll provision a dedicated cluster and run the stress test. ideally we do that after we finalize SSO and VPC peering to mirror production network conditions.
[05:00] Samir: timeline? we were hoping to decide by mid-August.
[05:05] Alex: that's doable. next two weeks: share artifacts, run stress test, security review; then exec review week of 2026-08-17.
[05:14] Jill: sounds good. please make the benchmark numbers easy for us  p50/p90/p95, tokens/sec, cost normalized to 1k tokens.
[05:22] Priya: we'll annotate the CSV with the exact environment: model build, sequence length distribution, GPU type, and provider image. note that the provider label in the raw CSV may be truncated or mis-encoded in the export.
[05:35] Alex: Any final concerns?
[05:38] Jill: just around SSO/SAML for admins and RBAC.
[05:42] Diego: we have SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC, i'll include docs and an admin contact.
[05:48] Alex: Great  recap next steps and who's owning what.
[05:52] Priya: Action items: push runs + configs, maybe a short technical deep dive next week if you want us to go line-by-line on the kernels.
[06:02] Samir: we'll probably take the deep dive, yes.
[06:05] Alex: meeting adjourned, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
